_meta.framework: Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills — Spanish Language Arts and Reading (SLAR)
_meta.citation: §128.7 (Grade 5) and §128.21 (Grade 6), adopted eff. 2017-09-25 (42 TexReg 5096), amended 2019-08-01 (44 TexReg 3858)
_meta.reviewNote: Verified 2026-09-17 against TEA ch128a.pdf and cross-confirmed with Cornell LII. IMPORTANT: §128.7 is codified in ENGLISH with authentic Spanish examples embedded — it is not a Spanish-prose translation of the ELAR TEKS. There is NO 'cognados' student expectation in §128.7(b)(3); cognates appear only in the non-binding introduction (a)(6). False friends are covered as 'commonly confused terms' under (b)(3)(E). 2026-10-28 cross-check: the full §128.7(b) knowledge-and-skills text was compared word-for-word between TEA ch128a.pdf (currently-in-effect, Aug 2019 update) and Cornell LII §128.7 — identical apart from one PDF line-break hyphen ('- logía'); §128.7 is TWO-SOURCE. Added §128.21 (Grade 6), likewise word-for-word identical between TEA ch128b.pdf and Cornell LII §128.21. In §128.21 the vocabulary strand is (b)(3) and response is (b)(7) (strand (b)(2) is beginning reading/writing). Scope note: Chapter 128 has NO Spanish Language Arts beyond grade 6 — §128.22/§128.23 are English Learners Language Arts (ELLA) grades 7–8 and Subchapter C (§§128.34–128.36) is ESOL I/II and ELDA, all English-language ESL courses, deliberately not stored here.

standards.subject: slar
standards.summary: Use context within and beyond a sentence to determine the relevant meaning of unfamiliar or multiple-meaning words.

standards.subject: slar
standards.summary: Identify the meaning of and use words with affixes (such as trans-, super-, anti-, semi-, -logía, -ificar, -ismo, -ista) and roots, including audi, crono, foto, geo, and terr.

standards.subject: slar
standards.summary: Differentiate between and use homographs, homophones, and commonly confused terms (such as porque/porqué, sino/si no, también/tan bien).

standards.subject: slar
standards.summary: Use context such as definition, analogy, and examples to clarify the meaning of words.

standards.subject: slar
standards.summary: Determine the meaning and usage of grade-level academic Spanish words derived from Greek and Latin roots, including metro-, grafo-, scrib-, and port-.

standards.subject: slar
standards.summary: Differentiate between and use homographs, homophones, and commonly confused terms (such as porque/porqué/por qué/por que, sino/si no, también/tan bien).
